_note: Single source of truth for the CORE panel-feed expression types. launch.py generates the agent-facing doc from this; components.js registers a renderer per `type`. Keep them in lockstep — test_panel.py asserts parity. Modules add their own types via their module.json `types` field, not here.

types.purpose: A replayable walk through code you read — kills the wall-of-text, makes your understanding auditable.
types.when: You read across several files and want the human to see HOW you understood the system (and catch a wrong turn).

types.purpose: The generic primitive: compose ANY one-off expression from fixed blocks — zero new code. Use this whenever no bespoke type fits; never invent a new type name.
types.when: The long tail — a status snapshot, a summary with evidence, a small report, a contextual ask. Reach for it before proposing a module.

input.why: the money flag deserves a second look

blocks: meter {label, value, max?, tone?, note?} — a magnitude/progress bar
badges {items:[{text,tone}|string]} — status chips at a glance
steps {items:[{label, state, note?}]} — sequence; state = done|active|pending|fail
callout {tone, text} — one emphasized line; tone = info|ok|warn|risk
coderef {file, lines?, note?} — a location in code
input {input:{...}} — an input-kit object; ALWAYS the last block(s), never above the evidence

types.purpose: A signed single-choice ask. Mark your recommendation with `rec` (an option id) + a one-line `why`; the human can override.
types.when: One real decision with a small set of named options. Never ask cold — put it after the trace/card that framed it.

example.why: you already query relationally in three places

types.purpose: Choose several from a set. `rec` is an array of ids; `min`/`max` bound the selection.
types.when: The answer is a subset, not one option (e.g. which platforms, which checks to run).

types.purpose: A free-text answer with YOUR proposed draft pre-filled — the draft IS your signature; the human accepts or edits it.
types.when: You need a sentence/name/value only the human can settle, but you can propose a strong default.

example.draft: Fixes crash on empty cart; faster cold start.

types.purpose: Pick a level on a small ordered scale (how urgent, how big). Use plain, everyday words for the levels — never codes. Sign your `rec`.
types.when: The decision is a degree, not a branch.

example.ask: How soon should we fix the login problem?
example.why: nobody can sign in until it's fixed

types.purpose: A STOP-tier approval gate. It does NOT queue with other picks — it posts ALONE the moment the human decides. Use for anything irreversible or money/publish-tier.
types.when: Store submit/publish, production release, spend, credential swap, destructive action. Asking IS the recommendation.

example.action: Submit Tavla 2.4.0 to App Store review?
example.detail: This is public and hard to reverse.

types.purpose: The files the HUMAN still has to touch, each with a reason. Not what you already changed — what you are handing them. This is the working set the panel opens for them.
types.when: You analysed a change and some of it needs a human hand (judgment, taste, a secret, a decision you shouldn't make). Name only those files; a worklist of everything is a worklist of nothing.

files.why: add the backoff here — the retry budget is a product call
surface the new error state; copy is yours

types.purpose: A layered architecture blueprint. `hot` highlights a node; `violation` draws a red arc for a layering breach.
types.when: Making an architecture point — showing layers/deps or flagging that a plan breaks them.

types.purpose: Phone mockups backing a visual/UX point.
types.when: Arguing a visual/flow change — show the shots, don't describe them.

types.purpose: Teach the codebase so the human's ownership survives even if the LLM is gone: tap a class -> plain what-it-is + what breaks if it fails.
types.when: Handing off understanding of a subsystem — a durable map, not a one-off explanation.
